$meta.description: Cross-page link ledger for the Line 2 (tier 2) mesh. Per tool: identity fields and the related-terms list — the primary artifact — with dispositions (linked with link records, or dropped with reason). Stores only cross-app linkage data not visible from any single file. Line 1 on-page anchors are intentionally NOT recorded here.

conventions.toolKey: kebab-case tool slug, matches the URL segment under /visual-tools/
conventions.relatedTerms: Built first, before any linking: page prose scanned against definitionsRepository + formulasRepository names (tool’s own section by default; cross-section matches only when topical), plus explicit "see the X page" gestures, plus each knowledge section’s central subject. Each term: entity (repo key or null), sections (occurrence slugs), status (linked | dropped | pending), links[] or reason.
conventions.completeness: A tool is complete when no relatedTerms entry has status "pending" and a re-scan yields no term missing from the list.
conventions.populationRule: Universal registry rule: ANY pass touching a tool page (any operation/tier) updates this registry as a by-product - at minimum identity + scanned terms as pending. Line 2 passes write the full dispositioned list. Existing Line 2 dispositions are only altered by Line 2 itself.

The tool shows its own inequality VIOLATED at its opening settings (mu = 10, variance = 4, a = 3, bound = 4/9 = 44.4%) for three of its nine distributions: exponential reports actual 77.6%, discrete uniform 57.9%, geometric 57.3%. Chebyshev's theorem is not violated - the tool is comparing a bound computed from the VARIANCE SLIDER against a distribution built from the MEAN ALONE. Six of the nine generators (exponential, poisson, binomial, geometric, negative binomial, hypergeometric) ignore `variance` entirely, so the plotted distribution's true variance is unrelated to the sigma^2 in the bound: exponential 100, geometric 90, discrete uniform 30, poisson 9.35, negative binomial 17.8, binomial 5.98, hypergeometric 2.75 - against a slider reading 4. Only normal and uniform honour it. Freezing these states would publish a still showing 'P(|X-mu| >= a) <= sigma^2/a^2' above a chart where actual exceeds bound. Resolving it is a design decision for the owner: either derive sigma^2 from the chosen distribution and drop the free slider (the six families fix the variance once the mean is chosen), or reparametrise each family to hit both the requested mean AND variance where that is possible. Awaiting that decision.
componentFix.resolution: Added an `effectiveVariance` derivation: the variance the PLOTTED distribution actually has. Normal and continuous uniform return the slider value unchanged (they are built from it); the other seven return their closed-form variance given the mean - exponential mu^2, poisson mu, binomial np(1-p), geometric (1-p)/p^2, discrete uniform (n^2-1)/12, negative binomial r(1-p)/p^2, hypergeometric with the finite population correction. `stdDev` now follows effectiveVariance so the plotting window is wide enough for the distribution being drawn, and the bound uses it too. The header panel prints the derived sigma^2 and, when it is derived, a one-line note saying the slider only sets sigma^2 for the normal and the uniform; the slider label says the same inline. ASSUMPTION STATED TO THE OWNER: the alternative - reparametrising each family to hit both a requested mean AND variance - is mathematically impossible for the Poisson and the geometric, which have one parameter, so deriving sigma^2 is the only option that works for all nine.

THREE WINDOW RULES worth recording because they are not visible from the parameters:
  - exponential: maxX = -ln(0.001)/lambda = 6.908, so its CDF ends at EXACTLY 0.999 by construction.
  - poisson: effectiveMax = max(30, ceil(lambda + 4*sqrt(lambda))) with an early break once the pmf drops below 1e-10; at lambda = 3 that stops at k = 19 and the 20 bars already sum to 1 in double precision.

line1.verification: STATIC ONLY - eslint parse of the page, the component and the diagrams module; slug/unit cross-check (15 sections, 15 objs defined, 4 units, no dupes, nothing missing or unwired); a node run of the diagrams module (10 SVGs, none malformed); a 30-literal evaluation pass confirming no LaTeX macro loses its backslash; and a separate geometry run confirming which region masks each layout actually draws. Region counts are the tool's own evaluator: 2 sets give A∩B 1/4, A∪B 3/4, A⊕B 2/4, Aᶜ 2/4; 3 sets give A∩B∩C 1/8 and (A∪B)ᶜ 2/8 (C alone plus the outside); 4 sets give A∩B 4/16 and 5 sets give A∩B∩C 4/32, both matching 2^(n-k).
line1.wiring:
B (export only), the cheapest pass in the project. The component ALREADY exported its expression parser and evaluator (parseExpression / evalNode), its region enumerator (buildRegionTable), its layout maker (defaultLayout / RELATION_LAYOUTS) and SET_NAMES. Only the three path builders (shapePath, rectPath, twoSetPaths) and DEFAULT_THEME / MATH_FONT needed adding to the export list - all pure module-level values, no behaviour change. So the stills are the tool's own geometry and its own region decisions, not a port. The page's Object.keys section generator with numeric ids was replaced with an explicit slug list.

Note: highlightFromExpression returns region KEYS, while the renderer needs the mask Set that the component's internal `evaluation` memo builds. The module reproduces that memo (parse once, evalNode per region) rather than using the exported helper.
line1.note:
PEDAGOGICAL FIND, verified against the geometry rather than assumed: the LAYOUT decides which regions have any area, while the region table is always 2^n rows. Checking which masks twoSetPaths actually returns a path for:
  Overlapping -> masks 0,1,2,3 (all four)
  Disjoint    -> masks 0,1,2 only; A∩B has NO path, so the expression selects the row and the diagram shades nothing
  A ⊆ B       -> masks 0,2,3; the 'A only' region does not exist
  A = B       -> masks 0,3 only; both 'A only' and 'B only' vanish
That gap between what an expression selects and what a diagram can show is the sharpest thing this tool demonstrates, and it is invisible in the live tool because you see one layout at a time. Two of the four units pair stills specifically to make it visible.

The 4- and 5-set layouts are fixed and dragging is disabled there, because no arrangement of four CIRCLES produces all 16 regions - the stills show the tilted-ellipse and five-fold arrangements the tool substitutes.
